data.gender_notes: Dalton is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old English 'dal' meaning 'valley' or 'dale', and 'ton' meaning 'town' or 'settlement'. This name was originally given to someone who lived in a valley. The name became popular in the Middle Ages due to Saint Dalton, a Welsh saint. In Scotland, it was a common name for clans living in valleys. The name Dalton carries the meaning “Valiant one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Dalton usually hope their child will grow to embody valiant one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

In Scotland, the name Dalton became synonymous with the Dalton Clans, powerful groups of people who lived in the valleys and worked together for mutual protection and support.

Saint Dalton is believed to have lived in the 6th century, and he is venerated as a patron saint of travelers, shepherds, and those who live in valleys. His story is one of faith, perseverance, and devotion to God, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of staying connected to our spiritual roots, even in the midst of the challenges and uncertainties of life. The name Dalton, therefore, offers a spiritual connection to the past, and it can serve as a reminder of the enduring power of faith and the importance of remaining rooted in our values and beliefs.
